parent_domains.justification: Single-cell multi-omics is a subset of single-cell data science, as it integrates various omics data at the single-cell level.
Single-cell analysis encompasses the study and examination of individual cells, which includes multi-omics approaches.
Computational biology is a broad field that includes the computational analysis of biological data, including single-cell multi-omics data.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Single-cell analysis is the closest parent domain as it directly involves analyzing various types of data, including omics data, at the single-cell level.

closest_child_domain.justification: Single-cell genomics specifically focuses on genomic analysis at the single-cell level, making it a subset of single-cell multi-omics.

sibling_domains.justification: Both single-cell genomics and single-cell multi-omics involve omics data but focus on different aspects. They share the same parent domain of single-cell analysis.
Single-cell sequencing involves various aspects of sequencing at the single-cell level, sharing techniques and methods with multi-omics.
Single-cell transcriptomics focuses specifically on the transcriptome, whereas multi-omics may involve additional omic data types.
This is a specific application of analyzing RNA at the single-cell level, similar in methodology and approach to multi-omics.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Single-cell genomics is the closest sibling domain as it directly involves the analysis of genomic data at the single-cell level, which is a significant component of multi-omics approaches.

unrelated_domains.justification: Cell biology generally focuses on the study of cells and their function but does not specifically involve computational or omics methods.
